items.readable_text:
Content:
The dot product (or scalar product) of two vectors [MATH: \mathbf{a}] and [MATH: \mathbf{b}] is defined as
[MATH: \mathbf{a} \cdot \mathbf{b} = |\,\mathbf{a}\,| \cdot |\,\mathbf{b}\,| \cdot \cos\theta,]
where [MATH: \theta] is the angle formed between the vectors when their tails are placed at the same point.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/9a97c3b428ac307511935a4c41a4fce0]

Content:
For example, suppose we know that [MATH: |\mathbf{a}|=2,] [MATH: |\mathbf{b}|=4,] and [MATH: \theta = \dfrac{2\pi}{3}.] We can now define the dot product (or scalar product) of [MATH: \mathbf{a}] and [MATH: \mathbf{b}] as follows:

Content:
[MATH: a ⋅ b|=|a|⋅|b|⋅ \cos θ; = 2 ⋅ 4 ⋅ \cos ((2π)/(3)); = 2 ⋅ 4 ⋅ (− (1)/(2)); = − 4]

items.title: Important Properties

sections.normalized_html: The dot product satisfies many properties that we would normally expect multiplication to satisfy. Given the vectors [MATH: \mathbf{a},\mathbf{b},\mathbf{c}] and any scalar [MATH: \lambda,] the following properties hold.
sections.readable_text: The dot product satisfies many properties that we would normally expect multiplication to satisfy. Given the vectors [MATH: \mathbf{a},\mathbf{b},\mathbf{c}] and any scalar [MATH: \lambda,] the following properties hold.

sections.normalized_html:
• The dot product distributes over addition: [MATH: (a + b) ⋅ c|= a ⋅ c + b ⋅ c; c ⋅ (a + b)|= c ⋅ a + c ⋅ b]

  • The dot product is associative with respect to scalar multiplication: [MATH: (λa) ⋅ b|= λ(a ⋅ b); a ⋅ (λb)|= λ(a ⋅ b)]

  • The dot product is commutative: [MATH: \mathbf{a} \cdot \mathbf{b} = \mathbf{b} \cdot \mathbf{a}]

Content:
The dot product satisfies many properties that we would normally expect multiplication to satisfy. Given the vectors [MATH: \mathbf{a},\mathbf{b},\mathbf{c}] and any scalar [MATH: \lambda,] the following properties hold.

Content:
- The dot product distributes over addition:
[MATH: (a + b) ⋅ c|= a ⋅ c + b ⋅ c; c ⋅ (a + b)|= c ⋅ a + c ⋅ b]
- The dot product is associative with respect to scalar multiplication:
[MATH: (λa) ⋅ b|= λ(a ⋅ b); a ⋅ (λb)|= λ(a ⋅ b)]
- The dot product is commutative:
[MATH: \mathbf{a} \cdot \mathbf{b} = \mathbf{b} \cdot \mathbf{a}]

lesson.readable_text:
Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
The dot product (or scalar product) of two vectors [MATH: \mathbf{a}] and [MATH: \mathbf{b}] is defined as
[MATH: \mathbf{a} \cdot \mathbf{b} = |\,\mathbf{a}\,| \cdot |\,\mathbf{b}\,| \cdot \cos\theta,]
where [MATH: \theta] is the angle formed between the vectors when their tails are placed at the same point.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/9a97c3b428ac307511935a4c41a4fce0]

Content:
For example, suppose we know that [MATH: |\mathbf{a}|=2,] [MATH: |\mathbf{b}|=4,] and [MATH: \theta = \dfrac{2\pi}{3}.] We can now define the dot product (or scalar product) of [MATH: \mathbf{a}] and [MATH: \mathbf{b}] as follows:

Content:
[MATH: a ⋅ b|=|a|⋅|b|⋅ \cos θ; = 2 ⋅ 4 ⋅ \cos ((2π)/(3)); = 2 ⋅ 4 ⋅ (− (1)/(2)); = − 4]

---

Item 2 — Example: Calculating the Dot Product of Two Vectors Given Their Magnitudes and Angle

Example Prompt:
For two vectors [MATH: \mathbf a] and [MATH: \mathbf b,] we have [MATH: |\mathbf{a}|=45,] [MATH: |\mathbf{b}|=12,] and the angle between the vectors is [MATH: \theta=77^\circ.] Find [MATH: \mathbf{a}\cdot\mathbf{b}] rounded to [MATH: 3] decimal places.

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
Using the formula for the dot product, we obtain:

[MATH: a ⋅ b|=|a|⋅|b|⋅ \cos θ; = 45 ⋅ 12 ⋅ \cos 77^{∘}; ≈ 45 ⋅ 12 ⋅ 0.224951; ≈ 121.474]

Item 5 — Example: Calculating the Dot Product of Two Vectors Given Their Magnitudes and Directions

Suppose that the vectors [MATH: \mathbf a] and [MATH: \mathbf b] are two vectors defined in the [MATH: x]-[MATH: y] plane. Explanation:
If [MATH: \mathbf{a}] makes an angle of [MATH: 127^\circ] with the positive [MATH: x]-axis and [MATH: \mathbf{b}] makes an angle of [MATH: -23^\circ] with the positive [MATH: x]-axis, then the angle between the vectors is

[MATH: θ|=|127^{∘} − (− 23^{∘})|= 150^{∘}.]

[IMG: /graphics/89fc54462c93d2e250ce6b87a97bbc8b]

Now, using the formula for the dot product, we obtain:

[MATH: a ⋅ b|=|a|⋅|b|⋅ \cos θ; = 4 ⋅ 3 ⋅ \cos 150^{∘}; = 4 ⋅ 3 ⋅ (− (sqrt(3))/(2)); = − 6sqrt(3)]

Item 8 — Tutorial: Important Properties

Content:
The dot product satisfies many properties that we would normally expect multiplication to satisfy. Given the vectors [MATH: \mathbf{a},\mathbf{b},\mathbf{c}] and any scalar [MATH: \lambda,] the following properties hold.

Content:
- The dot product distributes over addition:
[MATH: (a + b) ⋅ c|= a ⋅ c + b ⋅ c; c ⋅ (a + b)|= c ⋅ a + c ⋅ b]
- The dot product is associative with respect to scalar multiplication:
[MATH: (λa) ⋅ b|= λ(a ⋅ b); a ⋅ (λb)|= λ(a ⋅ b)]
- The dot product is commutative:
[MATH: \mathbf{a} \cdot \mathbf{b} = \mathbf{b} \cdot \mathbf{a}]

---

Item 9 — Example: Calculating Dot Product Expressions Using the Properties of the Dot Product

Example Prompt:
Find [MATH: (2\mathbf{a}-\mathbf{b}) \cdot \mathbf{c},] if [MATH: \mathbf{a} \cdot \mathbf{c} = 2] and [MATH: \mathbf{b} \cdot \mathbf{c} = -5.]

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
Using the properties of the dot product, we have:

[MATH: (2a − b) ⋅ c|= (2a) ⋅ c − b ⋅ c; = 2(a ⋅ c) − b ⋅ c; = 2 ⋅ 2 − (− 5); = 9]

Item 12 — Tutorial: The Dot Product of Perpendicular Vectors

Content:
Two nonzero vectors [MATH: \mathbf{a}] and [MATH: \mathbf{b}] are perpendicular if the angle between them is [MATH: \theta=90^\circ.] We can denote that two vectors are perpendicular using the symbol [MATH: \perp,] as follows:

Content:
[MATH: \mathbf{a} \perp \mathbf{b}]

Content:
In general, the dot product of two perpendicular vectors is [MATH: 0.] If [MATH: \mathbf{a} \perp \mathbf{b},] and [MATH: \theta = 90^\circ,] then

Content:
[MATH: a ⋅ b|=|a|⋅|b|⋅ \cos 90^{∘}; =|a|⋅|b|⋅ 0; = 0.]

Content:
The converse is also true. If [MATH: \mathbf a] and [MATH: \mathbf b] are nonzero vectors, then

Content:
[MATH: \mathbf{a} \perp \mathbf{b}
\quad\Leftrightarrow\quad
\mathbf{a} \cdot \mathbf{b} = 0.]

---

Item 13 — Example: Calculating the Dot Product of Perpendicular Vectors

Example Prompt:
Let [MATH: \mathbf{a}] and [MATH: \mathbf{b}] be two vectors with magnitudes [MATH: |\mathbf{a}|=13\sqrt{17}] and [MATH: |\mathbf{b}|=146,] and let the angle between the vectors be [MATH: \theta=\dfrac{\pi}{2}.] Find [MATH: \mathbf{a}\cdot\mathbf{b}.]

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
Since the angle between the vectors is [MATH: \theta = \dfrac\pi 2,] the vectors are perpendicular and thus [MATH: \mathbf{a} \cdot \mathbf{b} = 0.]

We can confirm this. Using the formula for the dot product, we obtain:

[MATH: a ⋅ b|=|a|⋅|b|⋅ \cos θ; = 13sqrt(17) ⋅ 146 ⋅ \cos ((π)/(2)); = 13sqrt(17) ⋅ 146 ⋅ 0; = 0]
